speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with episodes of painful urination. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or fever accompanying the knee pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome). The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle, now knee), urethritis (painful urination), high-risk sexual history, and the classic triad presentation strongly suggests this diagnosis, often summarized as "can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree." Given his age and symptoms, we should also rule out gonococcal arthritis with a NAAT and synovial fluid analysis to confirm the etiology and exclude septic arthritis.
